title: What is a Feedforward Neural Network?
description: How a feedforward network passes the input forward to a prediction and sends the error backward to update weights and biases.
content:
**Feedforward Neural Network (FNN)** is one of the simplest types of artificial neural networks. Its hallmark is that information flows in one direction - from the input layer, through hidden layers, to the output layer - without any cycles or feedback loops. This straightforward structure makes it a foundational concept in deep learning.

Structure:
• Input layer - receives the raw input.
• Hidden layers - transform the data step by step.
• Output layer - produces the final prediction.

**Forward propagation** - when an input is fed into the network, it passes through each layer sequentially:
• Each neuron in the hidden layers aggregates the incoming information and applies an activation function to introduce non-linearity.
• In the final layer, the transformed information is converted into the final prediction.

**Backward propagation** - once the output is produced:
• The network computes the error (residual term) using a loss function.
• The error is propagated backward through the network to update the weights and biases via an optimization algorithm - typically gradient descent combined with the chain rule.

Key idea:
• Forward propagation turns the input into a prediction.
• Backward propagation turns the error into better weights and biases.
